question: How many Bank of England MPC members will vote to raise Bank Rate at the December 17, 2026 meeting?

calls.reasoning: Nov 5 MPC hiked 3.75->4.00% 8-1 with Mann wanting 50bp; doves Taylor/Dhingra framed theirs as insurance/'one-for-now'. Reuters poll (Nov 13): 64/65 economists expect hold in Dec, next hike Feb; Scotiabank same. Markets diverge: Polymarket Dec 25bp hike ~73% ($110k vol), OIS reports 50-75%. Polymarket contract resolves on rate change not vote count — evidence, not anchor. I take P(hike)~45%. Hold => hike votes ~1-4 (Mann certain, maybe Greene/Pill/Lombardelli); hike => ~6-8 (Taylor/Dhingra may dissent), 8-9 (above 7.5 open bound) ~11%.
calls.dossier:
- Nov 5 2026 MPC: Bank Rate 3.75->4.00%, vote 8-1; all 8 for +25bp, Catherine Mann for +50bp (MTA, Scotiabank, Nov 5). First hike since Aug 2023; driver Iran-war energy shock, conflict in 9th month.
- Pre-meeting expectation had been 7-2 (hike vs hold); doves Dhingra and Taylor joined hike as 'insurance'; Taylor called it 'one-for-now' (Scotiabank, Nov 5).
- Member views (Reuters/Yahoo Nov 5): Bailey—argument for further increase conditional on energy; said consecutive hikes not predetermined, rejected 'two-and-done' commitment. Lombardelli—further hikes near-term absent disinflation; 'wouldn't rule December in or out' (each meeting live). Greene—more hikes 'likely'. Breeden—prolonged energy may require further tightening, demand weak. Ramsden—hike 'necessary now'. Pill—supported hike. Dhingra—wants evidence of pricing power before sustaining. Taylor—'up, down or sideways'.
- Reuters poll published Nov 13: 64 of 65 economists expect hold at 4.00% in Dec; next hike Feb 2027; median peak 4.25%. Scotiabank also expects Dec hold, Feb hike.
- Market pricing: swap markets moved to ~50% Dec hike odds right after Nov 5 (from ~30%) per Bloomberg; another source cites OIS ~75% as of Nov 12; Polymarket Dec-decision market favors a hike (contract on rate change, not vote count).
- CPI 3.5% Sep 2026 (11-month high); BoE projects inflation >4% early 2027, peak just under 5% Q2. Energy price cap +3.6% Oct 1. Bailey called recent oil drops 'good news'.
- Upcoming data: Oct CPI Nov 18; Nov CPI just before Dec 17 decision.
- Status quo: Bank Rate 4.00%; a hold would still likely include ≥1 hike vote (Mann's Nov stance).
- Resolution: count of MPC members voting to raise per Dec 2026 Monetary Policy Summary/minutes (votes for any size of rise count). Range -0.5 to 7.5, upper open (8 or 9 hike votes exceed range).
- Event window: single meeting Dec 17 2026; as of Nov 14 ~0% of window elapsed (decision is a point event, ~33 days away).
- Searched but not found: individual member speeches after Nov 5 beyond Lombardelli; Oct CPI outcome (not yet released).

calls.reasoning: Nov 5 2026 MPC hiked to 4.00% 8-1 (Mann for 50bp); Pill, Greene, Lombardelli signalled further near-term tightening, Taylor called it one-for-now, Bailey conditional on energy. Markets split sharply from economists: OIS ~75% and Polymarket December '25bps increase' 73% (~$110k total volume, contract matches the meeting but prices the decision, not vote count) vs Reuters poll 64/65 economists expecting a hold. Blended P(majority hike) ~0.57. In the hike scenario votes cluster 7-9 (8-9 lie above the 7.5 open upper bound, hence p_above_upper ~0.25); in the hold scenario Mann very likely dissents for a hike, possibly with Pill/Greene, giving 1-3. CPI on Nov 18 and energy prices are the swing factors.
calls.dossier:
- BoE MPC, meeting ending 4 Nov 2026 (announced 5 Nov): voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00%, first hike since 2023; Catherine Mann dissented for +50bp to 4.25%. Eight (Bailey, Breeden, Dhingra, Greene, Lombardelli, Pill, Ramsden, Taylor) for +25bp. No one voted to hold. (BoE minutes Nov 2026; leprivatebanker 5 Nov)
- Member guidance (mpamag recap, Nov 2026): Pill said the hike 'is unlikely to be sufficient', more tightening needed near term; Greene signalled more hikes likely needed; Lombardelli said there was likely a case for another increase 'in the near term', later said 'I wouldn't rule December in or out, February in or out'; Taylor called it a 'one-for-now' insurance hike and said the next move could be up, down or sideways; Bailey said absent news softening inflation risks he 'can see the argument for a further increase', depending on Middle East conflict and energy prices; Breeden, Dhingra, Ramsden gave no specific guidance.
- Reuters poll published 13 Nov 2026: 64 of 65 economists expect Bank Rate held at 4.00% in December; median next hike February 2027; most see a peak of 4.25%, a handful 4.50%.
- Market pricing reported around 12 Nov 2026: OIS/swaps implied about a three-in-four chance of a 25bp December hike (up from ~50% earlier in Nov and ~30% before 5 Nov). Danske and CBA expect hikes in Feb and Apr. A Polymarket December decision market exists (resolves on the decision, not the vote count); a Feb-2027 hike market also exists.
- Data: CPI 3.5% in September 2026 (11-month high); Ofgem cap up 3.6% on 1 Oct; BoE projects CPI above 4% early 2027, peak just under 5% (~4.9% mid-2027); Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q. Oct CPI release 18 Nov; more data late Nov. Oil prices fell recently (Bailey called it 'good news').
- Status quo: Bank Rate 4.00%. A hold would likely still see Mann (and possibly other hawks) vote to hike; a hike would likely see a large majority, with possible hold dissents from doves (Taylor, Dhingra).
- Base rates: in BoE cycles, the meeting after a new-cycle first hike often has split votes. 2021-22: Dec 2021 hike 8-1, then Feb 2022 hike 5-4 (4 wanted 50bp). Nov 2017 hike 7-2, then holds 9-0 for months. A hold meeting typically has 0-3 hike dissenters.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the BoE December 2026 Monetary Policy Summary/minutes vote tally (number voting to raise, including any who vote for a larger raise); if the meeting doesn't happen it resolves <1. Range is -0.5 to 7.5 with an open upper bound, so 8 or 9 hike votes land above the range.
- Event window: single meeting ending/announced 17 Dec 2026; as of 14 Nov 2026 about 0% of the event has occurred (one meeting, 33 days away).
- Searched but not found: direct OIS page content (rateprobability returned 403); any Kalshi/Manifold contract on the vote count; any member speeches after 12 Nov.

calls.reasoning: Nov 5 2026: 8-1 hike to 4% (Mann for 50bp; all 9 backed tightening). Markets (OIS 75-80%+, Polymarket Dec contract 25bp hike 74% on ~$110k volume, matching contract on decision not vote count) favour a December hike; Reuters poll (64/65 economists) expects hold until Feb, taken before Oct CPI. Blend to P(hike)~0.65. If hike: 6-9 votes, with Dhingra/Taylor most likely to dissent for hold; if hold: Mann plus 0-3 hawks (Greene, Lombardelli, Pill) vote to raise. 8-9 votes exceed the 7.5 upper bound, priced as p_above_upper=0.32.
calls.dossier:
- Nov 5 2026 MPC: 8-1 vote to raise Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00% (first hike since 2023); Mann voted +50bp to 4.25%. 25bp voters: Bailey, Breeden, Dhingra, Greene, Lombardelli, Pill, Ramsden, Taylor (BoE minutes / ActionForex, Nov 5).
- Member guidance Nov 5 (Yahoo/Reuters): Bailey sees argument for a further increase if pressures persist, then a more conditional approach; Lombardelli says a case for a further increase in the near term absent weaker inflation evidence; Greene says additional hikes likely required; Breeden says further tightening is more likely if energy stays high, depending on demand; Ramsden says the hike is necessary now; Dhingra wants clear evidence of pricing-power recovery before sustained higher rates; Taylor says next move could be up, down or sideways; Mann pushed for 50bp on credibility grounds.
- Lombardelli (mid-Nov): 'wouldn't rule December in or out, February in or out.'
- Reuters poll published Nov 13: 64 of 65 economists expect a hold at 4.00% in December; median sees the next hike in February and a 4.25% peak in 2027; some will wait for October CPI.
- Market pricing (TradingEconomics, ~Nov 13): OIS shows >80% odds of a December hike, up from ~50% at the start of that week; ~3 more hikes priced by mid-2027; 2y gilt 5.0%; strong GDP data; Brent's decline paused on Hormuz shipping tensions. Reuters also says futures are 'almost completely pricing in' December.
- Prediction market: Polymarket has a December BoE decision contract (resolves on the decision, not the vote count). Feb-2027 contracts also exist.
- Inflation: September CPI 3.5%; BoE projects >4% by early 2027 and a peak just under 5% (4.9% mid-2027); energy cap +3.6% Oct 1; ~20% fuel bill rise expected in January.
- Data before the meeting: October CPI on Nov 18; November CPI lands days before Dec 17.
- Status quo: Bank Rate is 4.00%; a hold means the count equals the number of hawkish dissenters (Mann the most likely).
- Base-rate notes: in past BoE cycles (2021-23), once a hike is delivered the vote count usually sits at 6-9 for raise; in holds during hiking phases, 1-4 members often dissented for a rise (e.g. Aug 2017 6-2 hold, 2023 holds 5-4 / 6-3).
- Resolution: resolves off the BoE December 2026 minutes' count of members voting to raise (any size counts); meeting not held -> <1. Question range tops out at 7; 8-9 votes fall above the upper bound (open).
- Event window: single meeting on Dec 17 2026; as of Nov 14, ~0% elapsed (the decision is a point event).
- Searched but not found: a member-by-member December vote prediction, and the rateprobability.com page (403).

calls.reasoning: Nov 5 MPC hiked 8-1 to 4.00% (Mann for 50bp). Markets (OIS 75-80% by Nov 13, Polymarket Dec 25bp ~73%) favour a December hike; the Reuters poll (64/65) expects a hold until Feb, and the MPC's conditional guidance (Bailey not predetermined, Taylor one-for-now) tempers market pricing. P(hike)~0.58. A hike most likely splits 7-2 with Taylor/Dhingra dissenting (8-9 votes ~40% conditional, so ~23% above the 7.5 bound); a hold gives Mann plus 0-3 hawks, i.e. 1-4 votes.
calls.reconciliation: Factual dispute: OIS-implied Dec hike odds (50% vs 75% vs >80%). Read as successive snapshots of a rising trend (30% pre-Nov 5, 50% just after, 75-80% by Nov 12-13 after strong GDP); latest taken as current, not re-verifiable without web access. Judgment: market vs economist split, weighed against member guidance (Bailey not predetermined, Taylor one-for-now) to P(hike)~0.58 - between Run 2 and Run 3, driven by the evidence not averaging. Vote split if hike: 7-2 modal given dovish framing by Taylor/Dhingra, so 8-9 at ~40% conditional, lower than Run 3's implied share. Hold: Mann near-certain hawkish dissent plus possible Greene/Pill/Lombardelli. Carried the runs' reference classes forward. No retrieval this run.
